# Graph slice: sources

Part of the graph. The full vocabulary is in `00-index.md`; the other slices
are `02-graph-*.md`. Every claim carries the video and timestamp it came from.

## source

### Adult Children of Alcoholics
*source · literature · anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

A free twelve-step programme Priebe recommends for inner-child and re-parenting work, noting it serves anyone raised in a dysfunctional family system rather than only those with alcoholic parents, and that its approach to inner parenting is unusually thorough.

  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles Setting Boundaries @560s — https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=560

### Brené Brown
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Shame researcher, cited here for the observation that shame cannot survive being witnessed — the premise underneath treating disclosure as the mechanism of repair rather than a by-product of it.

  - source: How Does An Anxious Attachment Style Develop? @1206s — https://youtu.be/EdpaCMW1PHw?t=1206

### Codependents Anonymous
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

A twelve-step programme Priebe recommends for both anxious-spectrum styles, noting she came to it sceptical of twelve-step work and changed her mind after reading the handbook. Its opening premise — that we are powerless over others — is the part she treats as decisive.

  - source: Attachment Styles And The Drama Triangle (Part 2) @820s — https://youtu.be/ynMNRFp68LM?t=820

### Coping With Trauma-Related Dissociation
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

The book Priebe credits for the phrase phobia of inner experiences, which she says clicked several things into place — the idea that a nervous system can develop an avoidance response to a feeling in the same way it would to an external threat.

  - source: Emotional Neglect: Healing From The Hidden Trauma Of What Didn't Happen @880s — https://youtu.be/lsBPvgnCJsQ?t=880

### Dan Siegel
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Interpersonal neurobiologist who coined the window of tolerance, the term this whole account of nervous-system wiring rests on.

  - source: Attachment & Nervous System Wiring 101: How Childhood Shapes Your Thinking and Self-Regulation @605s — https://youtu.be/sapNZnr9KYk?t=605

### Gabor Maté
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Named by Priebe, alongside Dan Siegel, Bowlby and Ainsworth, as the people to go to for real expertise. She states her own position plainly in this video: largely self-taught, currently doing a master's in attachment theory and research, writing a book and interviewing specialists, and not an expert — these videos are her working through what she is learning.

  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles Setting Boundaries @60s — https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=60

### John Bowlby
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Originator of attachment theory, and the source of the underlying claim this whole corpus rests on: that the need for a reliable other is a biological system rather than a preference.

  - source: Avoidant Attachment: When Attraction Turns Off Without Warning (Unpacking Deactivation Triggers) @245s — https://youtu.be/7mElEzMpbeE?t=245

### John Bradshaw
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Shame researcher whose work long predates the recent popular interest in the subject. Priebe takes the idea of shame-bound emotions from him: feelings that cannot be had without shame arriving fused to them.

  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Guilt Vs Shame @600s — https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=600

### Lundy Bancroft
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Runs anger-management programmes and wrote Why Does He Do That? Priebe quotes his line to people entering those programmes — that the problem is not an anger problem but an abuse problem — as the cleanest statement of the difference between having a feeling and what you gave yourself permission to do with it.

  - source: Fearful-Avoidant TRIGGERS: Managing The Shame Of Having Needs And The Guilt Of Taking Space @830s — https://youtu.be/QrhIWeLBkDQ?t=830

### Martin M. Broadwell
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Credited with the first description of the four-stage learning model in 1969, later restated by Curtis and Warren and popularised by Noel Burch at Gordon Training International as the four stages of learning any new skill. Priebe traces the attribution herself and notes the model was never intended for psychotherapy — she applies it because attachment healing is a learning process.

  - source: The 4 Stages Of Attachment Healing (Conscious Competency Model) @30s — https://youtu.be/GbWAlMQkWzo?t=30

### Mary Ainsworth
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Developed the Strange Situation, the procedure by which infant attachment was first categorised — and the source of the original lettered clusters that later acquired the names avoidant, secure and anxious.

  - source: How Does A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @58s — https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=58

### Nonviolent Communication
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core fearful-avoidant=alternating*

The system Priebe recommends specifically to avoidant-spectrum people learning to state a boundary: it works by going underneath irritation or overwhelm to the unmet need beneath, and by phrasing it so the other person can actually respond. Her argument is pragmatic — telling someone their feelings are unwarranted, even where true, does not produce the outcome you wanted.

  - source: The 4 Attachment Styles Setting Boundaries @900s — https://youtu.be/yPDW4GTl2C0?t=900

### Patricia Crittenden
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Worked under Ainsworth and developed the Dynamic Maturation Model, which treats the avoidant and anxious categories as gradients with sub-scales rather than boxes.

  - source: How Does A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Develop? @581s — https://youtu.be/_gCOo_vQM54?t=581

### Patricia DeYoung
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Author of Understanding and Treating Chronic Shame, which Priebe cites for its definition of shame as the sense of one's self disintegrating in the presence of a dysregulating other — the formulation that explains why shame and attachment fuse so early and so tightly.

  - source: Attachment Vocabulary: Guilt Vs Shame @300s — https://youtu.be/a9dptwMI2jg?t=300

### Radical Honesty
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

The practice Priebe credits with changing how she handles anger: expressing it clearly and cleanly at the moment it is felt, rather than carrying it in the body as resentment until it comes out all at once.

  - source: How The Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style Deals With Anger @790s — https://youtu.be/QFrkbdUIYFM?t=790

### Richard Schwartz
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Developed Internal Family Systems; Priebe calls No Bad Parts a brilliant introduction to it. The question she takes from him and uses constantly — ask the distressed part how old it thinks you are — is the hinge of this whole video.

  - source: Anxious Attachment: How to Find Your INNER ADULT When Triggered @340s — https://youtu.be/2lyyhVZDrss?t=340

### Ross Ellenhorn
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Author of How We Change (and Ten Reasons Why We Don't), which Priebe names as one of her favourite books. Its subject is the one she reaches at the end of this video: why behaviour we consciously want gone persists, because unconsciously it is paying for itself.

  - source: What To Do When You Mess Up (Attachment Healing) @1050s — https://youtu.be/31aWIy9jp5I?t=1050

### Scattered Minds
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

Gabor Maté's book on inattentive thinking and its links to a disorganised attachment system, which Priebe cites when discussing why fearful-avoidants so often reach for stimulation and large ambitions rather than sitting with pain.

  - source: 10 Signs You May Have A Fearful-Avoidant Attachment Style @3180s — https://youtu.be/5jk7PAa8D1o?t=3180

### Stephen Karpman
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Devised the drama triangle in the late 1960s, out of transactional analysis — the study of how unresolved childhood material gets projected onto present relationships.

  - source: Attachment Styles & The Drama Triangle (Part 1): Intro To The Drama Triangle @1s — https://youtu.be/4BrjQ9qX33k?t=1

### Thais Gibson
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=core anxious-preoccupied=core fearful-avoidant=core secure=secondary*

Runs the Personal Development School, where Priebe took courses. Priebe credits her as the first person she heard describe the avoidant spectrum as people with rich inner lives rather than as antagonists, and the deactivating-strategy vocabulary used across this corpus comes from that work.

  - source: What Are The 4 Attachment Styles? @1660s — https://youtu.be/AMUN9M9H3U4?t=1660

### The Betrayal Bond
*source · literature · dismissive-avoidant=alternating anxious-preoccupied=alternating fearful-avoidant=core*

A book Priebe cites not for its attachment content — she does not recall it addressing attachment directly — but as an illustration of how thoroughly a person can be adapted to exploitative environments, and of how reliably that adaptation delivers them into more of them.

  - source: Are Fearful-Avoidants Doomed To Have Dysfunctional Relationships? @752s — https://youtu.be/sUgQ_E24ma0?t=752
